clue.text: Captain possibly in command in present situation

indicators.note: the second in tells us one piece sits inside the other, the command abbreviation going within the gift word

parts.note: to present something is to offer it
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: A ship's captain is described as being in charge in the current state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'situation' rounds off the surface: the present that holds IC is OFFER. 'possibly' marks the definition as an example: a captain is one kind of officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain, in the army or navy, is one example of a commissioned officer.

clue.text: Some resistance found over taxing demands

definitions.meaning: units of electrical resistance are measured in this, named after a German physicist
letters from the British tax office were franked On Her Majesty's Service, abbreviated in initials

explanation.surface: Someone finds their opposition stiffened by a stack of tax bills.
explanation.walkthrough: On Her Majesty's Service was printed on British government mail, including tax demands.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of electrical resistance is the ohm, and initials stamped on official tax letters spell the same.

clue.text: Dry sherry and a bit of fish — nothing more

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A diner orders a dry sherry and just a morsel of fish, nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: Fino is a pale, very dry style of Spanish sherry.

clue.text: Diner imbibes fine new coffee ingredient

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: a diner is a cafe, a cheap eating place

indicators.note: new signals the letters of fine are made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: A customer at a cafe drinks some fine new coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diner' reads as a person eating, but it is the place; 'imbibes' is the container signal and 'new' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Caffeine is the stimulant compound naturally present in coffee beans.

clue.text: One is vertical in flight

parts.note: a flight of stairs has upright boards between the treads, which stand vertical while the treads lie flat

explanation.surface: An aircraft or bird is said to be flying straight upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests flying, but it is a flight of stairs; the vertical board of each step is the riser.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is the vertical part of a stair between two treads in a flight.

clue.text: Pack up quietly and clear out

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: out signals the letters of clear are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone silently packs their bags and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear out' reads as leaving, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on 'clear'.
explanation.definitionFit: To parcel something up is to wrap and package it, to pack it up.

clue.text: A fair land

parts.note: fair hair or skin is light in colour

explanation.surface: A fair is described as a country, or a land holding a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to come down and settle, as a bird lands on a branch.

clue.text: It may be thrown in car dispute that's unsettled

indicators.note: an unsettled arrangement of the letters is a disturbed one, so car dispute is reshuffled

explanation.surface: In an unresolved argument over a car, something gets thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's unsettled' signals an anagram of CAR DISPUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie full of custard is the classic slapstick missile hurled in a comedian's face.

clue.text: It's put out until eaten by a naval officer

indicators.note: put out signals the letters of until eaten are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is extinguished until a naval officer eats it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' signals an anagram of UNTIL EATEN; 'It's' and 'by a' merely join.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a commissioned rank in the navy, below a lieutenant commander.

clue.text: It's obvious the cargo's listing

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, the word means plainly evident
a ship's document listing the cargo and passengers carried

explanation.surface: It is plain that the ship's cargo is tilting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listing' suggests a ship leaning over, but here it means a list of the cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest means plainly evident, and a manifest is also the official list of a vessel's cargo.

clue.text: Sit out with a girl in gauzy fabric

indicators.note: out signals the letters of sit are put out of order

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone sits outside with a girl dressed in filmy cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit out' reads as staying outdoors, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on 'Sit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is a fine, thin, delicate woven material, a gauze-like cloth.

clue.text: Be there at the beginning and end

indicators.note: the beginning of the word the is its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to be present from the start to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the beginning' gives T, the first letter of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to be present there.

clue.text: Kind of talk more cordial than a tête-à-tête?

definitions.text: Kind of talk more cordial than a tête-à-tête?

parts.words: Kind of talk more cordial than a tête-à-tête?
parts.note: a tete-a-tete is literally head to head in French; swap the head for the organ of feeling and the conversation becomes warmer and more intimate

explanation.surface: A frank, warm conversation is compared to a private chat.
explanation.walkthrough: Tête is French for head, so a tête-à-tête is head-to-head; the heart is the seat of feeling, hence more cordial.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-to-heart is a candid, intimate conversation about personal feelings.

clue.text: The early morning air?

parts.note: air means a tune, and the tune heard at first light is the singing of birds together

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the freshness of the atmosphere at sunrise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' suggests the atmosphere; here it is a melody, the birdsong at daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: The dawn chorus is the singing of many birds together at daybreak.

clue.text: Letters sent off to a politician in the post?

indicators.note: sent off suggests the letters are dispatched, scattering them into a new order

parts.note: MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone posts letters to a Member of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent off' is the anagram signal; the definition plays on the post a street light stands on, not the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A street lamp is a light mounted on a tall post at the roadside.

clue.text: Dumbfounded by a dishonest arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement here is a fresh ordering of the letters of a dishonest

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked by a crooked deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' signals an anagram of A DISHONEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbfounded and astonished are synonyms, both meaning greatly amazed.

clue.text: Severe, in a way, on offence — not the first

parts.note: ST is street, a way

indicators.note: not the first tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for offence

parts.note: a wrong is an offence or injustice

explanation.surface: Someone takes a harsh view of a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' drops the opening letter of the offence word; 'in' and 'on' merely join.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong measures or language can be severe, harsh or forceful.

clue.text: Academic going through Russia

definitions.meaning: a university lecturer or fellow, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
a major river flowing through southern Russia to the Sea of Azov

explanation.surface: A scholar travels across Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Don is a great Russian river.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university teacher, and the Don is a river that flows through Russia.

clue.text: Have insufficient funds and don't finish the course

definitions.meaning: to lack enough money or supplies
a runner falling short of the full distance of a race

explanation.surface: Someone lacks the cash and so drops out of their studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests study, but the second sense is a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: To run short is to lack enough of something, and literally to run less than the distance.

clue.text: French-born

parts.note: the French word for born, used before a married woman's maiden name

explanation.definitionFit: Née is the feminine past participle of the French verb naître, meaning born.

clue.text: Order and routine for working organisation

indicators.note: to order the letters is to put them in a new sequence

explanation.surface: Discipline and habit are what make a company run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' signals an anagram of AND ROUTINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade union is an organisation of workers formed to protect their interests.

clue.text: Strained inspiration to produce a joke

definitions.meaning: breathing in with effort, making a whistling sound
a clever trick or prank, in British slang

explanation.surface: Laboured creativity is needed to come up with a gag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiration' suggests a creative idea, but it is a breath in.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheeze is to breathe with difficulty, and a wheeze is also British slang for a clever scheme or prank.

clue.text: Registry office used by cowboys?

parts.note: getting hitched means getting married, and cowboys tie up their horses at a rail outside the saloon

explanation.surface: Cowboys are imagined getting married in a register office.
explanation.walkthrough: A registry office is where civil marriages take place, and 'hitched' is slang for married.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitching post is a rail for tethering horses, comically seen as a place for getting hitched.

clue.text: The chaplain's walkabout

parts.note: to pad is to walk softly
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A clergyman goes walkabout among the people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walkabout' reads as one word, a royal stroll among crowds, but it splits into walk and about.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal title for a military chaplain.

clue.text: Parrot almost gets role in opera

indicators.note: almost means the word falls short by one final letter

parts.note: to parrot is to mimic

explanation.surface: A parrot lands a part in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter from MIMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème.

clue.text: There's a singular example of these in ancient history

indicators.note: in signals the letters are found inside the phrase ancient history

explanation.surface: A one-off instance of something turns up in old history.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'ancienT HIStory'.
explanation.definitionFit: The demonstrative pronoun used for one thing is the singular form of these.

clue.text: It bores me in the back

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: the rear is the back
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something tedious sits behind the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bores' suggests tedium, but it means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A reamer is a tool used to enlarge or finish a drilled hole.

clue.text: Caution had Simon dithering

indicators.note: dithering suggests confusion, so the letters of had Simon are jumbled

explanation.surface: Simon hesitates and is warned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dithering' signals an anagram of HAD SIMON.
explanation.definitionFit: To caution someone is to warn or admonish them.

clue.text: Private papers destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed suggests the papers are torn up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Confidential documents have been destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective about the papers, but it is the definition: a soldier of low rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is a soldier in the Royal Engineers; a private is the lowest army rank.

clue.text: Involves mending net before setting sail

indicators.note: mending the word net means reworking its letters
setting the word sail puts its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A fisherman repairs nets before heading out to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mending' turns NET into ENT and 'setting' turns SAIL into AILS.
explanation.definitionFit: If something entails a consequence, it involves or necessitates it.
